facts.text: The name Lake Orion can refer to the Village of Lake Orion or to the much larger Orion Township in Oakland County, of which the village is a part.
Lake Orion began as a resort town and over time took on elements of a bedroom community.
During Lake Orion's resort era, the Park Island amusement park was lit at night by strings of thousands of lights; the park closed in 1955.
The Lake Orion Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2006, surrounds the intersection of Broadway and Flint Street, historically the village's commercial center.
The historic district's commercial blocks are generally brick one- and two-story buildings, surrounded by wood-frame houses built from the mid-1800s to the mid-1900s.
Green's Park, off M-24 south of Flint Street, is the village's only park on Lake Orion and sits one block from downtown shopping and dining.
Bellevue and Park, the largest of Lake Orion's islands, are connected to the mainland by bridges and have year-round residents.
Children's Park, a downtown park with a gazebo and Paint Creek running through it, hosts the Downtown Development Authority's summer concert series and live events for Christmas and Halloween.
The Paint Creek Trail, which runs from Rochester to Lake Orion, and the Polly Ann Trail both reach Lake Orion.
Downtown Lake Orion opens the holiday season each November with the Sing and Stroll tree lighting ceremony in Children's Park; the 2025 ceremony was held on November 20.

hub.h1: Holiday Lighting in Lake Orion, MI
hub.intro: Lake Orion mixes a brick downtown, lake and island homes, and neighborhoods across Orion Township. Holiday Light Service brings full-service holiday lighting to homes, businesses and associations in the village and the township: design, installation with bucket trucks for the high work, upkeep through the holidays and takedown when they end. Every project begins with a free estimate.
hub.local_context: Lake Orion started as a resort town. In that era, the Park Island amusement park was lit at night by strings of thousands of lights, until it closed in 1955. Today the name covers both the Village of Lake Orion and the much larger Orion Township around it. The village's historic core, listed on the National Register in 2006, centers on Broadway and Flint Street, where brick one- and two-story commercial blocks are ringed by wood-frame houses built from the mid-1800s to the mid-1900s. Add year-round homes on Bellevue and Park islands, reached by bridge, and the lighting needs here run from storefronts to shorelines.
highlights: Rooflines, porches and tree wraps for the village's wood-frame homes and for houses across Orion Township
Building outlines and storefront lighting for the brick commercial blocks around Broadway and Flint Street
Permanent roofline lighting that lake and island homes can use all year, seen from the road and the water

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Lake Orion, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas lights for Lake Orion's village homes, island houses and township neighborhoods: designed, installed, serviced and removed. Free estimate.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Lake Orion, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: From century-old porches near downtown to lakefront eaves on the islands, we design the display, hang it with bucket-truck crews and remove it after the season.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Around downtown Lake Orion, the houses are largely wood-frame homes built between the mid-1800s and the mid-1900s. Their porches, gables and older eaves take patience: runs have to follow the trim, and fastening has to respect original wood. Out on the water, Bellevue and Park islands have year-round residents, and a lake home is seen from the shoreline and from the houses across the way, so the lakeside roofline and waterfront trees matter as much as the front. Across Orion Township the job shifts again, toward neighborhood rooflines and yard trees. Each setting gets its own design, and our crews take care of installation, upkeep during the season and takedown.
considerations: Houses near Broadway and Flint Street often date back a century or more. We keep the plan to the lines that define each one, like the porch, the main gable and the eaves, and choose attachment points on original trim with care.

Homes on Bellevue and Park islands are reached by bridge. Tell us about driveway space, parking and anything that limits where a truck can set up, and we will plan the install around it. If there is a dock or shoreline trees you want lit, point them out too.

Until 1955, the Park Island amusement park glowed at night under strings of thousands of lights. A home display can nod to that past with fewer, better-placed runs: a crisp roofline, a lit porch and one or two wrapped trees to anchor the yard.
faq: Is Orion Township included, or only the village?

Both. The Village of Lake Orion and the surrounding Orion Township sit well inside the Oakland County part of our service area, and that includes the year-round homes on Bellevue and Park islands. Wherever the house sits, the estimate starts with a design made for it.
When should I book Christmas lights in Lake Orion?

Book as early as you can. The install season typically stretches from October into early December, and the sooner you ask, the more dates are open. Downtown's Sing and Stroll tree lighting in Children's Park opens the season each November, which makes a good target for having your own home lit.
I live on the lake. What goes into my estimate?

Everything the plan needs: a design for the street side and the lake side, installation, service during the season and removal once the holidays end. Each roofline, tree and shrub in scope is listed, so you know what you are agreeing to before you decide.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Lake Orion, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Storefront and building lighting for downtown Lake Orion near Broadway and Flint Street, plus offices and HOA entrances in Orion Township. Free estimate.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Lake Orion, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Cornice lines, storefront windows and street trees for downtown merchants, plus entrance displays for property managers and associations, installed with bucket trucks.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Lake Orion works at a walking scale. The historic commercial center around Broadway and Flint Street is mostly brick one- and two-story blocks, a size where a lit cornice line, wrapped trees at the curb and glowing window frames can make a whole block feel like the holidays. People on foot see a display up close, so clean runs and tidy connections matter as much as brightness. Beyond downtown, we design lighting for offices, shopping centers, and subdivision and HOA entrances throughout Orion Township. Each commercial job covers the full season, from the first design to removal after the holidays.
considerations: Low brick blocks let a single roofline or cornice outline carry the whole facade. We plan runs to the building's lines, place fasteners on masonry with care, and add wrapped trees or window framing where a storefront needs more presence at street level.

Downtown's tree lighting in Children's Park opens the holiday season in November. If your storefront should be glowing that evening, request an estimate early, since storefront installs generally happen from October through early December and the earliest bookings have the most flexibility.

HOA boards and property managers in Orion Township can bundle entrance signs, boulevard trees and clubhouse rooflines into a single plan. The estimate itemizes each element, which makes a board vote simpler, and our crews handle installation, service and removal.
faq: Will lighting work on a historic building downtown?

It can, with planning. The Lake Orion Historic District surrounds the Broadway and Flint Street intersection, and we plan every attachment point and run around the architecture. If the building owner or the village has specific rules for the facade, share them up front and the design will work within them.
What about the street trees and poles out front?

Often possible, with permission. Street trees and lampposts along the sidewalk may be public property, so check with the village or the Downtown Development Authority first. Tree wraps and pole and lamppost decor are core parts of our work, and they can be planned alongside your building.
Do you light HOA and subdivision entrances in Orion Township?

Yes. Entrances for subdivisions and HOAs are a core part of our commercial work, along with shopping centers, offices and downtown districts. Send the entrance locations and a board contact, and each entrance will appear on the estimate with its own design and scope.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Roofline Lighting in Lake Orion, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: App-controlled permanent roofline lighting for Lake Orion lake, island and village homes, from summer evenings on the water to December. Free estimate.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Lake Orion, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Lights that stay on the roofline all year and answer to your phone, from a warm white glow on a summer night at the lake to full holiday color in December.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Lake Orion began as a resort town, and a home on the lake is still at its best on a summer evening. That is where permanent lighting earns its place. Installed once along the roofline, it stays put and runs from an app on your phone, so the look changes with the calendar instead of coming down after the holidays. For island houses on Bellevue and Park and for the older wood-frame homes near downtown, we map the layout to the roof and trim before anything is mounted.
considerations: Permanent lighting is not only for December. On a lake home, a soft warm line along the eaves makes evenings on the water and on the dock more inviting, and you can switch it on from the app without anyone stepping outside.

Wood-frame homes near Broadway and Flint Street can have mixed roof pitches, later additions and aging fascia. We look at the structure first and plan the mounting around it, so the lighting follows the home's lines and suits its age.

A permanent install on Bellevue or Park Island starts with access. Share how a truck reaches the house and where it can park, and we will plan the work so the lake-facing roofline gets the same finish as the street side.
faq: Where around Lake Orion do you install permanent lighting?

Across the village and Orion Township, from the older houses near Broadway and Flint Street to lake homes and island houses on Bellevue and Park. The free estimate starts with the roofline and the evenings you most want lit, and each run of lighting it covers is listed.
Is a lake house a good candidate for permanent lighting?

For many lake homes it is, because the lights earn their place in summer as much as in December. A warm accent along the lakeside roofline suits a summer weekend on the water, and the same run turns to holiday color once winter comes.
Besides Christmas, when would I use them?

Anything the calendar brings. Warm white works as an everyday accent, team colors suit game days, orange fits Halloween, and red, white and blue covers summer holidays. You change the look from an app on your phone, any night of the year.
